newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia stocks flat, await new government.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia stocks flat, await new government.

text.p: Slovenian shares ended barely changed on Wednesday and traders said no significant moves in prices were expected until the composition of the next government becomes known.
"Until the new government is formed shares will stagnate on poor turnover while investors wait for possible changes to Slovenian economic policy," one trader said.
Analysts said forming the new government may take several weeks as Slovenia's second general election on November 10 brought an undecided result.

Currently ruling Liberal Democrats emerged as the most successful single party with 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats, but are facing a loose rightist "Spring" alliance comprising three parties, which together received 45 seats.
Analysts expect prices to fall if "Spring" parties come to power because of their protective stand towards Slovenia's joining the EU.
The 10-share SBI index fell 0.52 points or 0.05 percent to 1,145.1. Overall seven shares fell, six rose, three remained unchanged, another eight were untraded and one was newly listed.
Turnover surged to 247.8 million tolars from 110.9 million.
Port Luka Koper, which listed its shares today, was by far the day's most active share but closed at 2,200 tolars, down from its opening price of 2,600. Turnover was 58,398 shares.
Traders said Luka's price came under pressure from profittaking as the opening price was way above the issue price of 1,390.
Market participants said Luka's price and volume in the future will largely depend upon whether the state, which owns 51 percent of the company's equity, would approve purchases by foreign investors.
"I expect the government will let foreigners buy up to 10 percent of Luka's equity," Toni Apollonio, an analyst of bank A banka, said.
Bank Hmezad was the day's leading decliner, falling 9.94 percent to 13,500 tolars on volume of only one share.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the biggest gainer, firming 6.11 percent to 15,940 tolars on volume of 61 shares for total turnover of 2.1 million tolars.
